sheets.noticed: 'June 1215' in big old-style type over a plain paper document. 'Rebel barons force King John to seal a charter'. History class video.
A wax seal stamps onto the bottom of the page. Small moment but it caught my eye.
'Runnymede' label, then the heading clears. Mostly just a page sitting there.
'Most of it: feudal fees and forests' in grey. Boring part, drifting.
Same page, then a yellow sticker pops up: 'But one clause will outlive everything else'. Okay, which one?
A couple of lines on the page get highlighted yellow. I want to see what it says.
Camera zooms into the highlighted lines and the seal. Quiet pause.
Page shrinks back and 'No free man shall be imprisoned' appears right on top of the page and the seal, the seal circle sits behind the word 'imprisoned'. Messy but readable.
'except by the lawful judgment of his peers' adds below. Lots of words on screen now.
Yellow sticker 'or the law of the land.' That's the line I'll remember.
Text clears back to the page with the seal. 'A king...'
'A king', 'IN WRITING' off to the side, then 'THE LAW' sticker drops in above the king.
'THE LAW' on top, 'A king' greyed underneath. Got it: the king is under the law.

remembers: In 1215 the barons made King John seal the Magna Carta, and one line said no free man can be jailed except by his peers or the law of the land, which put even the king under the law.
